Subject: Renewal health: usage & capacity options for Velvet Commerce

Hi Samira / Aaron —

Quick note ahead of the renewal: I pulled Q2 usage and performance metrics to give a concise picture of where things stand and what levers we can use to make the next term smoother for Velvet Commerce. Attached are the raw numbers (usage_q2_velvet_2028.xlsx) and the latency report (latency_report_q2.pdf).

Top-level summary:
- Avg daily token consumption (Q2): ~18.2M tokens/day (30% QoQ growth).
- Peak concurrency: spiky around 10–11am PT; sustained 12k reqs/hr at peak.
- Latency incidents: three brief degradations tied to a specific model variant during batch window (details in latency_report).
- Cost impact: current run-rate projects a ~21% overage relative to the committed baseline without changes.

What we recommend for renewal/options to reduce risk:
1) Staged uplift + burst credits: modest committed increase (10–15%) with a burst credit allowance for seasonal peaks. This preserves unit pricing while providing runway for growth.
2) 24-month term with a pricing band: 8–10% pricing discount in exchange for extended term and a small minimum uplift commitment.
3) Routing/variant policy: pin high-latency paths to a stable variant and enable automatic fallback — engineering can implement within a week.

Ask: can we schedule a 30-min executive brief next week (propose Tue 7/25 at 11:00am PT) to walk the numbers and agree on a mutual action plan? If useful, I can send a draft MAP (mutual_action_plan_draft.docx) in advance.

Thanks —

Thanks Samira — quick answers below and a proposed MAP attached.

1) Latency incidents: customer-facing 504s (search timeouts) occurred during two peak windows (June 8 and June 29). Root cause: an emergent model-variant memory overhead + a brief autoscaler lag during a large batch reprocessing job. We mitigated with a variant pin and short autoscaler tuning; longer-term fix is kernel selection update (ETA 10 days with our infra team). See page 3 of latency_report_q2.pdf for the incident timeline.

2) Modeled cost per 1M tokens:
- Current committed baseline: $16.20 / 1M tokens (effective after existing discount).
- Staged uplift scenario (+12% committed, 20% burst credit): $15.10 / 1M tokens (net effective).
- 24-month term with uplift (12% min uplift): $13.65 / 1M tokens (10% term discount applied).

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
- Week 0: Exec brief + agree on uplift band and burst credit.
- Week 1–2: Engineering sync to apply variant pin + routing fallback.
- Week 2–4: Apply autoscaler tuning and deploy kernel selection patch to the affected model.
- Month 1: Post-change readout and new health dashboard cadence (weekly for 4 weeks).

I've attached the draft MAP (mutual_action_plan_draft.docx) with checklist items and owner assignments. For the exec brief I've proposed Tue 7/25 11:00am PT — does that work for you and Aaron? Sean / Marissa: will you join to cover escalation terms and pricing?

If you want formal pricing numbers in a short table, I can ask finance to provide a one-page quote for the three scenarios.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
